title: Repository Compose teardown safety governance
purpose: Define safe, reset, and destructive Compose teardown policy classes with confirmation expectations while preserving proof evidence, generated-report boundaries, and fail-closed validation behaviour.

coveredIssues.title: Compose teardown safety
coveredIssues.completionBasis: This artefact classifies safe, reset, and destructive teardown actions and records confirmation expectations. Dependency USF-386 is Done.

safeActions.evidenceRule: read-only inspection must not alter proof or evidence state

safeActions.actionClass: stop running services without deleting state
examples: leave artifacts and evidence in place
safeActions.confirmation: safe default when command scope is explicit
safeActions.evidenceRule: accepted proof evidence, raw evidence, and generated reports remain untouched

examples: clear service state that is classified as rebuildable
resetActions.confirmation: explicit reset mode plus dry-run summary before mutation
resetActions.evidenceRule: raw proof evidence and accepted proof artifacts must be collected or explicitly out of scope before reset

resetActions.confirmation: explicit reset mode with clear list of changed resources
resetActions.evidenceRule: unknown resource ownership must block reset or fall back to safe stop

destructiveActions.actionClass: remove volumes or persisted service data
destructiveActions.confirmation: owner-approved policy plus explicit human confirmation
destructiveActions.evidenceRule: must not delete evidence or audit material required for a proof claim

destructiveActions.actionClass: delete proof artifacts or evidence-adjacent outputs
destructiveActions.confirmation: blocked by default; requires separately authorised retention or pruning policy
destructiveActions.evidenceRule: raw evidence and accepted proof evidence are protected by default

confirmationExpectations.expectation: May run with explicit scope and no destructive side effects.
Requires dry-run summary, explicit reset mode, and evidence-preservation notice.
Requires owner-approved policy, explicit human confirmation, protected-path checks, and no unresolved evidence dependency.

validationProofExpectation: Future implementation must prove cleanup preserves required evidence.
Future implementation must prove reset restores test state when reset is the claimed behaviour.
Future implementation must fail closed when resource ownership, evidence relevance, provider mode, or environment classification is unknown.
Future implementation must keep stale, missing, blocked, timeout, and unknown outcomes as non-pass states.
protectedResources: generated reports whose source evidence is still required

acceptanceCriteriaTrace.criterion: Teardown policy classifies safe, reset, and destructive actions with confirmation expectations.

nonClaims: This artefact does not implement Compose teardown, reset, clean, or destructive commands.
This artefact does not delete evidence, artifacts, volumes, generated reports, or service state.
This artefact does not make a Test, Staging, production, deployment, live-provider, or readiness claim.
This artefact does not approve high-risk destructive cleanup.
